strengths: Addresses a genuine and important gap: existing user simulators are agent-friendly but unrealistic for real-world deployment
Well-grounded taxonomy of non-collaborative behaviors informed by marketing research, dialogue studies, and real user data
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple models (GPT, Qwen, LLaMA) and benchmarks (MultiWOZ, τ-bench) with detailed failure analysis
Clever architecture that balances goal-aligned behavior with non-collaborative behavior simulation using dialogue state tracking and ending verification
Insightful finding that agents trained only on collaborative data become MORE vulnerable to non-collaborative behaviors
Practical and extensible framework demonstrated on additional benchmarks (ColBench, MINT)
Extensive documentation including all prompts, implementation details, and dialogue examples enabling reproducibility
Realistic scenarios testing multiple simultaneous non-collaborative behaviors
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: primarily extends prior work (Yao et al. 2024) with straightforward augmentations (goal generation, style transfer, truncation, LLM-based checking)
Somewhat expected findings: that agents degrade under non-collaborative conditions is intuitive; limited guidance on architectural changes for robustness
Moderate human evaluation results: ~60% win rate only marginally better than chance; tangential behavior scores notably lower in combined settings
Incomplete behavior taxonomy: only 4 types; excluded toxic content; unnatural behavior combinations not fully addressed; unclear distinction from prior underspecification work
Test scenario selection concerns: MultiWOZ excludes retrieval tasks with weak justification (89 scenarios only); τ-bench excludes 8 human-transfer scenarios with observed excessive transfers
Goal alignment verification bias: regeneration until success could make problems appear easier; relies on GPT-4o-mini judge (MCC=0.77)
Limited baseline comparisons: only PBUS baseline; no adversarial dialogue approaches; no component ablations
Arbitrary experimental choices: 30-step limit validation indirect; only 4 trials per scenario; 50-step analysis shows inconsistent improvements
